subject.title: [Bug]: exec tool silently corrupts 2>&1 / 2>/dev/null shell redirect arguments

question: Should #87980 stay open as an exec command-corruption bug until a current-main repro identifies the mutation boundary, or be closed as unsupported allowlist redirection behavior?
rationale: Source inspection narrows likely paths but does not prove either a current-main fix or a current-main failure, and the report's examples can be confused with adjacent exec approval policy.

options.title: Keep For Repro
options.body: Keep the issue open and require a focused current-main repro or regression test before any fix PR is queued.

options.title: Close As Policy
options.body: Close only if maintainers decide the observed cases are actually the documented allowlist redirection restriction rather than command corruption.

options.title: Fold Into Policy Work
options.body: Link to #95331 or #96475 only for the allowlist-policy subset while leaving command mutation evidence to a separate bug.

recommendation.title: Keep For Repro
recommendation.body: Keep the issue open and require a focused current-main repro or regression test before any fix PR is queued.

likelyOwner.reason: They are the strongest current history signal across exec schema/runtime and adjacent redirection matching code.
